svg.title: Two servers merged into one catalog, with the colliding name qualified on both sides
svg.desc: On the right, two terracotta servers publish their tools. The first, system-info, publishes get_system_info, find_process, terminate_process and watch_cpu. The second, mini, publishes find_process and ping. The name find_process is marked as colliding on both servers. In the middle, a catalog counts every name across every server before it names anything: find_process is seen twice and is qualified on both sides, never one, so the server listed first cannot silently win; everything else is seen once and keeps its bare name, which is what the server's own documentation calls it. Every tool is also registered under its qualified form, so a name from an earlier turn still resolves. On the left is the single flat list the model is shown, the only shape a provider tool interface accepts, with the two qualified names marked in the margin and four names left alone. Underneath, two callouts. The first is about the separator: a dot is inside the legal character set for a tool name, a slash is outside it, and an illegal name is rejected at the catalog, naming the server, rather than at a provider's interface. The second is about dispatch: the model asks for the qualified name, the catalog resolves it to a server and a bare tool name, and what the host sends on the wire is the bare name, because the server has never heard of the qualified form. A closing note says the prefix must come from the key you gave the connection in your own configuration file, and that shadowing, where one tool silently vanishes, is a strategy to recognize rather than copy.
svg.text: Qualify only what collides, qualify both sides, and use a dot because a slash is not a legal character in a tool name.
